text: Vegetable harvesting (ការប្រមូលផលបន្លែ) should be based on the crop's maturity, the intended buyer, and how long produce will take to reach the consumer -- there is no single harvest stage for all vegetables. Leafy vegetables (បន្លែស្លឹក) are generally harvested while tender; cucumber (ត្រសក់), eggplant (ត្រប់), okra, and tomato (ប៉េងប៉ោះ) should be harvested to match the buyer's requirements for size, firmness, color, and maturity. During hot dry-season (រដូវប្រាំង) conditions, harvest during the cooler morning to reduce heat exposure and water loss. During the wet season (រដូវវស្សា), muddy fields and frequent rain make cleanliness and careful handling especially important. Harvest gently with clean hands or tools, use clean containers without overloading (crushing at the bottom damages produce), and separate diseased, rotten, or bruised produce from marketable produce immediately. Do not assume cold-chain infrastructure is available -- for produce going to a nearby village market, the practical priority is harvesting at the right market maturity, keeping produce shaded, and selling quickly; for a distant market, coordinate harvest timing with the buyer and transport schedule, since vegetables sitting hot for hours lose quality before arrival. Harvest for the market actually being sold to, not simply when the vegetable looks largest -- 'fully ripe' is not always 'best for selling.' Do not name one universal best harvest stage or dominant variety for Preah Vihear; ask the farmer what vegetable and variety they're growing and who the buyer is before giving specific advice, since harvest maturity depends heavily on the destination market.
